rows.name: Micro servo TowerPro SG90 with a printed arm or flap

dims_mm.notes: The same purchased SG90 as SERVO_SG90_TOWERPRO. x = across the mounting tabs, y = case width, z = base to the top of the horn (Rapid/TowerPro drawing: case 22.2 x 11.8 mm, 16 mm base to the tab line). In the shell the case sits behind the wall, centred on the feature position, with the output shaft 5.9 mm toward local +u; the horn and the printed arm or flap are outside.

mount.hole_origin: left end of the tab span on the servo centreline, top view
mount.notes: Two tab holes about 27.8 mm apart (estimate, not on a drawing read). The shell has two printed bosses with 1.6 mm pilot holes for the two self-tapping screws supplied with the servo; screw size UNVERIFIED (physical check).

module_connector.location: lead exits the case end; 3-way 2.54 mm female servo plug

backplane_harness.mapping: electrical.py maps module pins to slot pins by name (see backplane-v1 slot pin 'accepts'); the servo's own 2.54 mm plug needs an XH-3 to servo-plug adapter lead (made to drawing)

aperture.notes: 8 mm hole for the output shaft and the horn hub (horn hub size UNVERIFIED); the printed arm turns outside, parallel to the face.

electrical.notes: 150 / 700 mA is the SG90-class planning figure the power budget used before (no datasheet current found)

firmware.driver_notes: LEDC 50 Hz on the J_LED signal (GPIO2 through the 74AHCT1G125 buffer): gs_board.cpp servo_write, moved non-blocking by gs_motion.cpp (wave on tap, open on a schedule). No library.

kicad.notes: J_LED (the only 5 V port): a design has this servo or an addressable LED, not both.

uncertain: running/stall current not found from a primary source: 150/700 mA is a planning figure, not a measured current

port.why: J_LED is the only 5 V port: 5 V supply and a 5 V PWM signal from the buffered GPIO2. A design can have an addressable LED or a servo, not both. Stall current spikes on USB 5 V: never let the arm stall against a stop.

prompt_rules: A servo arm or flap (SG90 or MG90S) can wave, point, lift a flag or open a small flap on a schedule or a tap. It replaces the LED on the only 5 V port. Portion size and flow through a flap are a physical check, never promised.

Place the servo as a feature on a flat part of a side or the front: its 32 x 12 mm case sits behind the wall centred on `at`, and the printed arm (40 mm) or flap (label it 'flap': 40 x 30 mm) turns outside, up to 90 degrees either side of pointing up. Keep buttons out of that sweep. Never in a child-directed design.
